researchConclusion: The constitutional, bonded-labour, criminal, rescue/prosecution and rehabilitation frameworks overlap and cannot safely be reduced to a customer-facing bonded/forced-labour classifier or allegation intake. Keep this feature on governance fallback until qualified legal and safeguarding review approves a source boundary and a non-identifying organisational-control model.

sourceInventory.title: The Constitution of India 2026 — Article 23
sourceInventory.publisher: Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice
sourceInventory.notes: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar and other similar forms of forced labour. It is a constitutional boundary, not a product classifier.

sourceInventory.title: Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976
sourceInventory.publisher: Ministry of Labour and Employment / India Code
sourceInventory.notes: Provides bonded-labour-system definitions, abolition, bonded-debt consequences, implementing authorities, Vigilance Committees and offences.

sourceInventory.title: Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Rules, 1976
sourceInventory.notes: India Code records the Rules dated 28 February 1976. Exact controlled file acquisition remains pending.

sourceInventory.title: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 — sections 143–146
sourceInventory.publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs / India Code
sourceInventory.notes: The current criminal-law source separately covers trafficking, exploitation of trafficked persons, slavery and unlawful compulsory labour. Product logic must not collapse these offences into the Bonded Labour Act route.

sourceInventory.title: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer-2021
sourceInventory.notes: The scheme was approved for FY 2021-22 to 2025-26. Its annexures contain highly sensitive individual and case data that is prohibited from product/provider capture.

sourceInventory.title: Standing Committee on Labour, Textiles and Skill Development — Fifteenth Report, 2026
sourceInventory.notes: The Committee records that the 2021 rehabilitation scheme is being merged with the Labour Welfare Scheme for 2026-27 to 2030-31 and recommends a detailed post-merger operational plan. The product must not infer that plan.

sourceInventory.title: NHRC Advisory 2.0 to Identify, Release and Rehabilitate Bonded Labourers
sourceInventory.notes: Current NHRC advisory listings continue to surface the 8 December 2021 advisory. It is safeguarding/administrative guidance, not an automated legal classifier.

sourceInventory.title: Standard Operating Procedure for Identification and Rescue of Bonded Labourers and Prosecution of Offenders — Ministry letter dated 14 May 2026
sourceInventory.notes: NHRC July 2026 materials expressly direct authorities to follow this Ministry SOP, but the exact Ministry-hosted source file has not yet been acquired. This is a hard activation blocker.

sourceInventory.title: Prajwala v. Union of India & Ors. — 2026 INSC 609
sourceInventory.notes: Use only for qualified constitutional/jurisprudential mapping. It must not be converted into a bonded-labour or trafficking classifier.

hardBlockers.requirement: Acquire and fingerprint the exact Ministry of Labour and Employment SOP referenced as issued by letter dated 14 May 2026.

Acquire the notified/approved 2026-27 to 2030-31 Labour Welfare Scheme and detailed post-merger bonded-labour rehabilitation operational plan before representing current rehabilitation workflow, eligibility or amounts.
Qualified counsel must map Article 23, the 1976 Act/Rules, BNS sections 143–146, current Supreme Court jurisprudence and State/authority process without collapsing distinct legal tests.
Approve a human-only escalation path for live allegations, rescue, threat, retaliation, trafficking, confinement, violence or other immediate safeguarding concerns outside the RAG/provider route.
Approve collection minimisation, access, retention, deletion and incident-handling controls before any future case-adjacent data can be contemplated.
Review State/UT implementation, Vigilance Committee, District Magistrate and rehabilitation-fund operational variations before any jurisdiction-specific workflow.

prohibitedData: caste, community, sex/gender or other protected-characteristic data
recruiter, creditor, alleged captor or accused identity
debt amount, debt instrument or repayment narrative
wage, payroll, attendance or bank/DBT data
movement restriction, document retention or confinement narrative
violence, threat, retaliation, coercion or abuse narrative
complaint, rescue, FIR, case, prosecution or court material
victim or witness identity or statement
